chunks: “There is no harm in wiping in wudu (ablution), forward and backward.”

As for his statement, “and he wipes his head and his feet with the moisture of his hands without taking fresh new water,” the two previous reports indicate this. This is because the report of Zurārah from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام includes at its end: “Then he wiped his head and his feet with the remainder of what remained in his hand, and he did not return it to the vessel.” Likewise, the other report narrated by Zurārah along with his brother Bukayr from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام has at its end: “Then he wiped his head and his feet up to the ankles with the excess moisture of his two palms, and he did not renew water.” This is explicit in dropping the obligation of taking new water for wiping, as you see, and this is also indicated by that.

What al-Shaykh narrated from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-ʿAbbās, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.بِفَضْلِ كَفَّيْهِ: with the excess moisture of his two palms
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, the part wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.رِجْلَيْهِ: his feet, the limbs wiped in this ruling

ai.seo_question: Must fresh water be taken for wiping the head and feet in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This text discusses the fiqh of wiping in wudu (ablution), specifically that wiping the head and feet should be done with the remaining moisture on the hands rather than with newly taken water. It also indicates that wiping may be done forward and backward, and cites earlier reports from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام as proof for this ruling.
